title: Owning a Home
description: Tax, insurance, repairs, the HOA, and the risk in borrowing your equity.
wolfLine: The mortgage is the payment you expected. The rest is the year you live.

property-tax.definition: A tax from your local government based on what your home is worth. Owners pay it. Renters pay it only inside the rent.
property-tax.example: A $3,600 yearly bill is $300 a month.

escrow.definition: An account the lender uses to collect property tax and homeowners insurance along with the mortgage, then pay those bills for you.
escrow.example: A $1,400 mortgage plus $300 of tax and $100 of insurance is an $1,800 payment into the loan and the escrow.

homeowners-association.definition: A homeowners association. It charges a fee and sets rules for the neighborhood or the building. The fee is on top of the mortgage.
homeowners-association.example: An HOA fee of $250 a month is $3,000 a year.

home-equity.definition: What you own in the house: its value minus the loans against it.
home-equity.example: A home worth $320,000 with a $240,000 loan has $80,000 of equity.

heloc.definition: A home equity line of credit. You borrow against the equity, and the house is the collateral. If you cannot pay, you can lose the house.
heloc.example: Borrowing $20,000 of an $80,000 equity stake leaves $60,000 if the value stays put.

lessons.title: Property Tax
lessons.summary: The bill comes from the town, not the bank.

steps.title: A local bill
steps.body:
[[Property tax]] is based on the home’s value. This home’s bill is **$3,600** a year. That is **$300** a month.

There is no single national rate. Use the bill, not a rumor about “what tax usually is.”

steps.prompt: The yearly property tax is $3,600. What is that per month?
You set aside $300 a month. After 12 months, how much have you set aside?
Who sends the property tax bill?
steps.explain: The town or county assesses it. The lender may collect it, but the tax is not the lender’s fee.

steps.prompt: Renters never feel property tax, because only owners are billed.
steps.explain: Owners are billed. Landlords fold the tax into the rent.

lessons.title: Insurance and Escrow
lessons.summary: The lender often collects the tax and the premium for you.

steps.title: One payment, three jobs
steps.body:
Homeowners insurance here costs **$1,200** a year, so **$100** a month. The [[deductible]] is **$1,000**. The [[premium]] is the yearly price.

[[Escrow]] adds that **$100** and **$300** of tax to a **$1,400** [[mortgage]] payment. You pay **$1,800**, and the lender pays the tax and the insurance when they come due.

steps.prompt: A $1,200 yearly premium is how much per month?
Mortgage $1,400, tax $300, insurance $100. What is the full monthly payment?
On this loan, where does each bill get paid from?
steps.explain: Tax and insurance ride in the payment. The HOA and the repairs do not.

steps.prompt: Escrow means the tax and the insurance are free.
steps.explain: You pay them every month inside the $1,800. Escrow only changes who holds the money until the bill is due.

lessons.title: The 1% Sketch
lessons.summary: A rough jar for the things that break.

steps.title: One percent, as a sketch
steps.body:
A common sketch is to set aside about **1%** of the home’s value each year for maintenance. On a **$300,000** home, that is **$3,000** a year, or **$250** a month.

A new roof can cost more than a year of that jar. The 1% is a starting point, not a quote.

steps.prompt: What is 1% of a $300,000 home?
What is that $3,000 per month?
The water heater costs $900. How much of a $3,000 jar is left?
The 1% sketch is the most a repair is allowed to cost.
steps.explain: It is a savings target. A repair can cost more, which is why the jar exists before the break.

lessons.title: The HOA Line
lessons.summary: It is easy to budget the mortgage and miss the fee.

steps.title: A third bill
steps.body:
An [[HOA|homeowners-association]] fee is not part of the mortgage and not part of escrow. On this statement it is **$250**.

**$250** a month is **$3,000** a year, on top of the **$1,800** you already counted for the loan, the tax, and the insurance.

steps.prompt: Which line is the HOA fee?
steps.explain: It is the $250 line. Escrow did not include it.

steps.prompt: What is this whole October statement?
What is the HOA fee for a year at $250 a month?
An HOA fee is optional once you have already closed.
steps.explain: If the home is in the association, the fee is part of owning it. Read it before you offer.

steps.title: The stake
steps.body:
[[Home equity]] is the home’s value minus the loans against it.

Worth **$320,000**. Loan **$240,000**. Equity **$80,000**. If the value falls and the loan does not, the equity shrinks.

steps.prompt: The home is worth $320,000 and the loan is $240,000. How much equity is that?
The value falls to $300,000 and the loan is still $240,000. How much equity is left?
Which event raises your equity if the value stays the same?
steps.explain: Principal reduces the loan. Interest and the deductible do not.

steps.prompt: Equity is cash in your checking account.
steps.explain: It is a stake in the house. Turning it into cash means selling, or borrowing against it.

lessons.title: A HELOC
lessons.summary: Borrowing the equity puts the house on the line.

steps.title: The house is the collateral
steps.body:
A [[HELOC]] lets you borrow against [[home equity]]. This example borrows **$20,000** of an **$80,000** stake.

The old mortgage is **$240,000**. After the draw, you owe **$260,000**. If the value stays **$320,000**, equity left is **$60,000**. Miss the payments and you can lose the house.

steps.prompt: The mortgage is $240,000 and you draw $20,000. How much do you owe in total?
The home is still worth $320,000. How much equity is left after that draw?
What is the risk that a credit card does not have?
choices: The lender can take the house
You must sell the house to open the line
steps.explain: The house is the collateral. That is the difference.

steps.prompt: A HELOC is a gift of your equity, so there is nothing to pay back.
steps.explain: It is a loan. The equity is the collateral, not a present.

lessons.title: A Housing Jar
lessons.summary: Give the repair jar a number before the year spends it.

steps.title: Five hundred dollars
steps.body:
You set aside **$500** a month for the house beyond the mortgage payment. The 1% sketch says maintenance wants at least **$250** of that.

The rest can go to a project or a roof jar. Every dollar gets a job.

steps.prompt: Set aside $500. Maintenance needs at least $250. Assign every dollar.
steps.explain: Maintenance gets at least $250. All $500 is assigned.

steps.prompt: Maintenance takes $250 of the $500. How much is left for the project and the roof jar together?
The roof jar gets $100 a month. How much is that in a year?
Once the mortgage is paid this month, the housing budget is finished.
steps.explain: The mortgage does not include the HOA, the repairs, or the roof jar.

lessons.title: Nia’s First Year
lessons.summary: The surprise was a bill she could have read at closing.

story.title: Nia’s first year
story.body:
Nia is 33 and a graphic designer. Her home is worth **$250,000**. She saved the 1% sketch, **$2,500**, and felt ready.

The water heater died in March and cost **$900**. That fit in the jar. The [[HOA|homeowners-association]] fee did not. It is **$200** a month, **$2,400** a year, and she had budgeted **$0**.

The repair jar was never going to pay the association. She adds the fee to the monthly housing number before she calls the year a success.

steps.prompt: What is 1% of Nia’s $250,000 home?
The water heater is $900. How much of the $2,500 jar is left?
The HOA fee is $200 a month. What is that for the year?
She tries to pay the $2,400 HOA from the $1,600 left in the repair jar. How short is she?
steps.explain: $2,400 − $1,600 = $800. The fee needed its own line.

steps.prompt: What should next year’s budget do with the HOA?
choices: Give it a monthly line of its own
Hope the repair jar covers it
steps.explain: A fee you can see at closing is not a surprise. It is a bill.

lessons.title: Sharpen Up
lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Owning a Home
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: Property tax is $4,800 a year. What is the monthly set-aside?
A home is worth $280,000 and the loan is $200,000. How much equity is that?
Which bill is the house itself on the line for?
steps.explain: The HELOC uses the house as collateral.

steps.prompt: An HOA fee is included in a typical mortgage payment.
steps.explain: It is a separate bill. Read it before you buy.
